newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices inch up on cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices inch up on cooler weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for April inched up slightly Tuesday, boosted by forecasts for colder Midwest and eastern weather this week though gains today were more modest than on Monday.
Traders said favorable spreads also continued to encourage early injections, but some noted longer term-bearish implications, particularly with storage already comfortable.
"Early injections mean if you put it in on the front end, you could lose on the back end," said one Houston trader.
Louisiana Gulf Coast swing gas firmed a couple of cents to the $1.95-2.00/mmBtu area, more than 15 cents over April 1.

Appalachian and eastern city gate prices scored the greatest gains on the approaching cold. Below-normal temperatures were forecast for the eastern half of the nation for much of the week. Columbia moved to the high-teens from the $2.10-2.15 area on Monday, while New York city gate prices again jumped more than 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s.
Midcontinent prices, still buoyed by cooler weather there, edged up slightly to the high-$1.80s, 15 cents above April indices. Northern at Demarc broke into the low-$2 area.
In south Texas, prices were up several cents to the low-$1.90s, while west Texas gas gained a similar amount to the low-$1.80s.
At the southern California border, spot prices were four cents higher at about $1.90.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA gas stock report ranged from a draw of five bcf to a build of 30 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks fell by 15 bcf.
